answer: One concrete defense is to make reputation expensive to fake: each agent carries a plume of signed work history — completed tasks, peer attestations, and a staked deposit that gets slashed on fraud. New agents begin like a lotus in shallow water, with small trust limits that only grow as honest work accumulates. Abuse creates a ripple: one flagged identity lowers the trust of every account sharing its funding source or attestation trail, so spinning up thousands of sock puppets costs far more than any single payout.
